1. Core Clinical Tension: A 43-year-old woman presents with recurrent upper abdominal pain, cholestatic transaminitis, mildly elevated CA 19-9, and a periampullary mass seen on transabdominal ultrasound and MRCP. While the presentation is highly concerning for primary periampullary adenocarcinoma, endoscopic ultrasound reveals that mechanical pancreatic duct obstruction is caused by an intraluminal adult helminth coexisting with an ampullary polyp.
2. Admission Breakpoint: Admission triage ends following history, physical exam, liver biochemistry, CA 19-9, transabdominal ultrasound, and MRCP showing the periampullary lesion. Endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) and ERCP worm extraction mark the confirmatory intervention.
3. Differential Distinctions: Isolated periampullary adenocarcinoma was the leading initial diagnosis, but EUS demonstrated that ductal obstruction was complicated by a live parasitic worm. Choledocholithiasis or pancreatic lithiasis presents with acoustic shadowing on ultrasound rather than non-shadowing parallel linear echogenic strips.
case_prompt: A 43-year-old woman presented with recurrent upper abdominal pain of 3 years' duration, which had notably increased in frequency over the preceding year. She had no significant co-morbidities. Physical examination was unremarkable. Baseline laboratory evaluation revealed a normal leukocyte count, elevated serum alanine transaminase (289 IU/L), aspartate transaminase (328 IU/L), and alkaline phosphatase (468 IU/L), with a mildly elevated CA 19-9 level of 47.3 U/mL. Transabdominal ultrasonography and subsequent magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) demonstrated an ill-defined heterogeneous mass measuring 10 x 14 mm in the periampullary region.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: The periampullary mass on MRCP and elevated CA 19-9 pointed to primary periampullary malignancy as the sole cause of ductal dilation and symptoms, but endoscopic imaging revealed an intraluminal parasite inside the pancreatic duct.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) demonstrated a similar finding ill-defined heterogeneous mass (10 x 14 mm) in the peri-ampullary region. Duodenoscopy revealed a bulky ampulla with a small area of the overlying friable nodular mucosa. Histopathological examination suggested a tubulovillous adenomatous polyp with foci suspicious of adenocarcinoma.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Recurrent biliary-pancreatic colic with elevated canalicular enzymes suggested ductal calculi, but imaging showed an elongated non-shadowing tubular structure rather than calcified shadowing stones.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: showed infiltration of the duodenal wall and terminal common bile duct and a long, linear, nonshadowing echogenic strips in a dilated pancreatic duct (PD)

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Endoscopic ultrasound revealed characteristic long, linear, non-shadowing echogenic strips within the dilated main pancreatic duct representing an adult Ascaris lumbricoides worm, which was subsequently extracted via ERCP prior to oncologic resection.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) was done to assess feasibility of ampullectomy, showed infiltration of the duodenal wall and terminal common bile duct and a long, linear, nonshadowing echogenic strips in a dilated pancreatic duct (PD) suggestive of an adult A. lumbricoides worm inside the main PD [Figures 1 and 2]. Patient underwent endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography [Figure 3] for extraction of the dead worm and deworming was done subsequently.

editor_comments: Admission narrative strictly maintained prior to duodenoscopy, EUS, and ERCP extraction. Zero pathogen spoilers. Direct quotes verified.
